reproduction_target: Discovery of human neural enhancers for cis-regulatory therapy (CRT) of neurodevelopmental-disorder (NDD) haploinsufficiency: NDD risk-gene prioritization by de novo variant burden (denovolyzeR), candidate cis-regulatory element (cCRE) assembly from five published enhancer-gene prediction datasets (UCSC liftOver, bedtools merge, promoter/exon filtering), ABC-score enhancer-gene mapping (ENCODE ATAC/ChIP pipelines, TrimGalore, Bowtie2, Picard, ABC MakeCandidateRegions.py / run.neighborhoods.py / predict.py with HiC and pcHiC), lentiMPRA library design (44,312 tiles over 5,425 cCREs) and MPRAflow association + count processing, DESeq2 differential RNA-vs-DNA barcode analysis in R, FlashFry-based design of a 15,643-gRNA piggyFlex CRISPRa library, CellRanger preprocessing of a 200,517-neuron multiplex single-cell CRISPRa screen, gRNA-to-cell assignment and MOI calculation (BSgenome matchPattern), SCEPTRE calibration and discovery testing parallelized with Snakemake, Homer motif enrichment, biochemical-mark enrichment with bigWigAverageOverBed, VISTA transgenic-enhancer overlap (Fisher's exact test), Gviz locus visualization, and qPCR/luminescence validation statistics. All bench work - oligo-pool synthesis and library cloning, iPSC/NGN2-iNeuron differentiation, lentivirus production and transduction, piggyBac nucleofection and selection, 10x Chromium capture, Illumina sequencing, cerebral organoids, patient iPSC lines, humanized-hTcf4 mouse fibroblasts and transgenic mouse embryos - is wet-lab (W, OOS for computational reproduction).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, derived from the Methods prose of the bioRxiv JATS XML (WebFetch returned HTTP 403; curl with a browser user-agent returned 200 and 257,537 bytes; title phrase 'cis-regulation therapies' and 'neural enhancers' verified present in the fetched file, so no cross-paper swap occurred). The paper carries both a Data Availability and a Code availability statement in the main text. Code coverage per step was determined from the GitHub repository's file listing (GitHub REST tree API, 25 blobs) and its README prose only - no script was opened or read line-by-line, per Stage-1 rules. env_capture_class is 'n/a' everywhere and the verdict ceiling is RI. 12 wet-lab steps counted in W and not verdicted.

steps.label: NDD risk-gene prioritization: 466 genes compiled from DD/ASD/schizophrenia/Tourette association studies plus DDG2P clinician-curated genes, then de novo variant burden across 42,320 offspring (8,251 protein-truncating, 33,442 missense, 10,973 synonymous variants) compared to expectation with the denovolyzeR tool; 337 genes with observed/expected de novo LoF > 1 retained. Code present in repo (Gene_Prioritization_for_CRISPRa_Cis_Regulation_Therapy.R). No denovolyzeR version, no R version stated for this step, and the input de novo variant tables are cited by reference only with no accession or download URL

Read processing of the epigenomic inputs to ABC: GW18 human prefrontal cortex and 7-8 week NGN2-neuron ATAC-seq and H3K27ac ChIP-seq aligned to hg19 with the 'Encode Consortium ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq pipelines with default settings and pseudo replicate generation turned off'; NGN2 reads hard-trimmed to 50 bp with TrimGalore '--hardtrim5 50' (github.com/FelixKrueger/TrimGalore); CUT&RUN reads aligned with Bowtie2 v2.3.5.1 '--local --very-sensitive-local --no-mixed --no-discordant -I 10 -X 700'; duplicates removed with Picard MarkDuplicates v2.26.0 '--REMOVE_DUPLICATES=true --ASSUME_SORTED=true'. Exact pins on Bowtie2 and Picard but not on the ENCODE pipelines or TrimGalore; no environment closure; no script for this step in the repo; source ATAC/ChIP data cited by reference (only the pcHiC contacts carry an accession, GSE113483)

Activity-By-Contact enhancer-gene mapping: hg19 promoter regions from Gencode basic annotation (protein-coding transcripts, 500 bp or 2000 bp upstream of TSS, isoform promoters overlapping >1 bp merged); ABC MakeCandidateRegions.py with '--peakExtendFromSummit 250 --nStrongestPeaks 150000'; run.neighborhoods.py on the cCREs plus merged transcript bounds; predict.py with '--hic_type bedpe --hic_resolution 10000 --scale_hic_using_powerlaw --threshold .02 --make_all_putative' using GW17-18 fronto-parietal 10 kb HiC (score > 0) or NGN2 pcHiC from GSE113483. Repo carries ABC_Score_Analysis_and_Candidate_Enhancer_Selection.R. Flags are fully specified but no version for the ABC model code and no GENCODE release number is given

cCRE assembly and prioritization: enhancer-gene predictions combined from five published developing-brain datasets (correlation-based sc-multiome mapping, ABC on NGN2 bulk ATAC, ABC on GW18 PFC bulk ATAC, Cicero co-accessibility on GW14-20 scATAC, ABC on GW17-21 scATAC); GW18 PFC and NGN2 predictions converted to hg38 with UCSC liftOver; filtered to the 337 CRT candidate genes; all cCREs extended from center to at least 500 bp and combined with 'bedtools merge'; any cCRE overlapping a 2000 bp promoter region or a protein-coding exon removed; 5,425 unique cCREs retained. Code present (ABC_Score_Analysis_and_Candidate_Enhancer_Selection.R). No version for liftOver or bedtools, no liftOver chain file version, and the five source datasets are cited by reference with no accessions

lentiMPRA library design: 44,312 x 270 bp tiles densely covering the 5,425 cCREs with 90 bp overlaps, plus 100 active / 99 inactive NPC MPRA controls, 729 active / 600 inactive HAR controls, and base-level shuffled versions of a random subset; 46,340 unique designs total (Table S3). Code present (MPRA_Library_Design_and_Analysis.R); designed sequences tabulated in the supplement. No software version for the design step and the random-shuffle subset selection has no reported seed

CRISPRa gRNA library design: NGG protospacers identified and scored with FlashFry 'using default parameters'; TSS-distance metric from human fetal brain 5' CAGE (FANTOM FF:10085-102B4, CTSS, hg38, URL given); genome-wide CRISPRa design rules for optimal TSS distance; enhancer gRNAs prioritized toward element center; polythymidine / extreme-GC gRNAs excluded; six iterative rounds of selection with 'successively relaxing score and distance thresholds' to keep the top 4 gRNAs per TSS and per enhancer; 1,500 NTCs and extra TSS gRNAs taken from the Horlbeck CRISPRa-V2 library; 15,643 gRNAs final (Table S4). Repo has Scaled_Screen_gRNA_Design.Rmd and Scaled_Flashfry_Cluster_Enhancers.txt / _Promoters.txt. No FlashFry version, and the six relaxation thresholds themselves are not enumerated in prose

MPRA association-sequencing processing: 'Association sequencing data was processed using MPRAflow v2.3.5 association.nf utility with default parameters', producing coords_to_barcodes.pickle and a final complexity of 9,338,288 barcodes across 44,729 cCREs. Exact version pin on MPRAflow and defaults for all parameters, but the tool is external and no MPRAflow config/profile file is deposited in this paper's repository; no Nextflow version, no container digest, no conda spec. Input raw sequencing deposited on the IGVF portal (IGVFDS1120GRVG, released)

MPRA DNA/RNA barcode counting: DNA/RNA barcode sequencing plus coords_to_barcodes.pickle used as input to the MPRAflow v2.3.5 count.nf utility with default parameters. Same situation as C7 - version pinned, parameters defaulted, but no deposited workflow config, no Nextflow/container/conda pin. Raw and processed data on the IGVF portal (IGVFDS1120GRVG)

MPRA differential-expression analysis: 'Downstream MPRA analysis was performed using R v3.4.2 in RStudio v2023.06.1+524'; MPRAflow DNA/RNA barcode counts combined across sequencing batches and tested with DESeq2 using sequencing batch as a covariate; active oligos defined as FDR < 0.01 and log2FoldChange > 1 (empirical FDR 6.2% from the scrambled-negative-control count distribution). Interpreter pinned exactly (R v3.4.2, RStudio v2023.06.1+524), thresholds fully specified, code in the repo (MPRA_Library_Design_and_Analysis.R plus Fig_2_Viz.Rmd), data released on the IGVF portal. DESeq2 itself carries no version and there is no lockfile/renv.lock/container, so version stays at 1 by the Stage-1 rule (exact pins without environment closure)

Single-cell CRISPRa screen preprocessing: 'Sequencing data were processed with CellRanger v7.0.1. FASTQs were generated with cellranger mkfastq (default parameters), and gene expression matrices with cellranger count against the GRCh38-3.0.0 reference transcriptome (10X Genomics, default parameters).' Cells with >20% mitochondrial reads or <900 UMIs excluded; 200,517 neurons retained. Both the tool version and the reference-transcriptome version are pinned exactly, defaults declared, QC thresholds given, and the exact invocations are deposited (NovaSeq_cellranger_mkfastq_command_line.txt, NovaSeq_cellranger_count_command_line.txt, NovaSeq_cellranger_aggr_command_line.txt). Data released on the IGVF portal (IGVFDS2290SSEF). No container digest or conda lock, so version capped at 1

gRNA spacer coordinate isolation and gRNA-to-cell assignment: hg38 genomic coordinates for final gRNA spacers obtained with 'a loop built around the matchPattern() function from the BSgenome package'; a global UMI filter of 5 gRNA UMIs per cell used to assign gRNAs to single-cell transcriptomes; neighbouring-gene isolation for each gRNA. Code deposited (SCEPTRE_Scaled_Neuron_Preprocessing_&_MOI_Calculation.Rmd, gRNA_Mapping_neighbouring_gene_isolation_Scaled_Screen.Rmd). No version for BSgenome, the BSgenome hg38 data package, or R at this step

Single-cell CRISPR screen differential-expression testing with SCEPTRE: covariate matrix built from gRNA and gene-expression library size (total UMIs), unique genes in both libraries, 10X lane and percent mitochondrial reads; genes within a 2 Mb window (1 Mb up/downstream of each gRNA) isolated with construct_cis_pairs(); run_calibration_check() and run_discovery_analysis() run one-sided with default parameters; gRNAs/cCREs first tested against predicted target NDD genes, hits then tested against all genes within 1 Mb; NTCs tested against the same gene set and randomly downsampled for QQ visualization; SCEPTRE P-values Benjamini-Hochberg corrected with a 0.1 cutoff. 'Custom R and snakemake scripts were used to partition tests and parallelize processing' - deposited as SCEPTRE_Discovery_Pair_Generation.Rmd, SCEPTRE_snake_V2.r, Snakefile and sm_script.sh. No version for SCEPTRE, snakemake or R at this step, and no seed for the NTC downsampling

Transcription-factor motif enrichment: MPRA active oligos supplied to Homer v5.1 findMotifsGenome.pl with a 270 bp window size and inactive oligos as background; presence/absence of each motif per cCRE identified with findMotifsGenome.pl '-find' over all Homer annotated motifs followed by annotatePeaks.pl per motif instance; cCREs containing a given motif averaged by log2(RNA/DNA) count ratio. Homer version pinned exactly; window size and background fully specified; but no Homer script or command file is deposited in the repository (only the downstream Fig_2/Fig_3 visualization Rmds), and the Homer annotated-motif database release is not stated

Biochemical-mark enrichment: activity of each biochemical marker computed across 258 ATAC-seq and histone/transcription-factor ChIP-seq datasets using bigWigAverageOverBed from the UCSC Genome Browser; values averaged for corresponding marks across datasets and brain regions and correlated with MPRA log2(RNA/DNA) count ratios. The 258 datasets are cited by three literature references with no per-dataset accession list and no download manifest; no bigWigAverageOverBed version; no script for this step in the repository; the averaging and correlation method (correlation type, filtering) is described only in outline

In vivo transgenic-enhancer concordance: validated active human enhancers from mouse transgenic assays (VISTA Enhancer browser, cited) separated by tissue and overlapped with cCREs containing an oligo in the top 10% of MPRA activity; odds ratios of transgenic neural-tissue activity given strong MPRA activity computed by Fisher's exact test. Downstream visualization code present (Fig_3_Viz.Rmd); no VISTA release version or download date, no overlap tool or version named, and the overlap criterion (bp of reciprocal overlap) is not specified

Locus-level visualization of screen results: single-cell CRISPR screen differential-expression P-values plotted alongside tracks for cCREs, target-gene links, iPSC-derived neuron ATAC-seq, H3K27ac and RefSeq validated transcripts (ENSEMBL/NCBI) using the Gviz package. Figure code deposited (Fig_4_Viz.Rmd, Fig_S4_Viz.Rmd); underlying data released on the IGVF portal. No Gviz version, no R version at this step, and no release/date for the RefSeq / ENSEMBL annotation used for the transcript track

Validation-assay quantification and statistics: qRT-PCR fold-changes in HEK293T, patient iPSC lines, cerebral organoids and humanized-Tcf4 mouse fibroblasts analysed by the comparative CT method with normalization (Eif4a2 for fibroblasts), and Nano-Glo luminescence normalized to negative-control lentivirus; reported as fold-changes with q-values (e.g. 1.1-fold, q = 0.008; 1.3-fold, q = 0.01). Figure code present (Fig_5_Viz.Rmd, Fig_S5_Viz.Rmd). No statistical test named for the q-values, no multiple-testing procedure stated, no software version, and the raw Ct / luminescence tables are not covered by either IGVF accession (which are MPRA and scCRISPRa file sets)

lentiMPRA library construction: 46,340-design oligo pool synthesized by Twist Bioscience, two-step PCR with Kapa HiFi to add 15 bp transcribed barcodes, Gibson assembly into linearized pLS-SceI (Addgene 137725), I-SceI background digestion, electroporation into NEB 10-beta E. coli, plating, colony whole-plasmid sequencing (Plasmidsaurus) and ZymoPURE II midiprep

piggyFlex CRISPRa gRNA library cloning: Twist oligo pool double-stranded by low-cycle Q5 PCR, Gibson assembly into piggyFlex, triplicate electroporation into NEB 10-beta, amplicon sequencing on an Illumina NextSeq 2000 for balance QC, SapI double digestion and Gibson insertion of the puromycin and GFP selection cassettes, quadruplicate re-transformation and re-sequencing

Individual lentiviral gRNA construct cloning: annealed IDT oligos golden-gate cloned with BsmBI-V2 into lentiGuide-Hygro-dTomato (Addgene 99376) or pLV hU6-gRNA hUbC-VP64-dCas9-VP64-T2A-GFP (Addgene 66707), transformation, miniprep and whole-plasmid sequencing confirmation

Lenti-X HEK293T culture, lentivirus production (EndoFectin transfection, TiterBoost, 0.45 um filtration, Lenti-X concentrator, 1500 x g harvest) and qRT-PCR titering; generation of a stable dCas9-VP64 HEK293T line by high-MOI transduction with lenti-EF1a-dCas9-VP64-Puro (Addgene 99371) and puromycin selection

WTC11 NGN2-iNeuron differentiation for MPRA: doxycycline-inducible NGN2 at AAVS1, StemFlex maintenance, 3-day pre-differentiation in KnockOut DMEM/F-12 with N-2, NEAA, NT-3, BDNF and laminin, then BrainPhys maturation with B-27, half-media change without doxycycline at day 7

Single-cell CRISPRa screen cell engineering: 16 million WTC11 NGN2-dCas9-VPH iPSCs nucleofected with the gRNA library and piggyBac transposase at 5:1 molar ratio (Lonza 4D, P3, CB-150), 20 ug/mL puromycin selection for 7 days, then NGN2 induction and 19-day neuronal maturation with 20 uM trimethoprim to stabilize the ecDHFR-dCas9-VPH, with a minP-tdTomato reporter check of CRISPRa function

lentiMPRA transduction and library preparation: magnetotransduction of NGN2 neurons with ViroMag R/L at mean MOI 46 across 3 replicates, DNA/RNA extraction (QIAshredder, AllPrep, TURBO DNase, SuperScript III), two-round indexing PCR with 16 bp UMIs, and custom sequencing on Illumina NextSeq 550 (association 2x150 Mid-Output; barcode counting 1x75 High Output) by Novogene

Single-cell library preparation and sequencing: neuron dissociation, FACS enrichment of the top 10% piggyFlex GFP signal, capture on 10x Genomics Chromium Next GEM Chip M with the Single Cell 3' HT v3.1 Dual Index kit and Feature Barcode CRISPR chemistry (CG000418 Rev C), 16 lanes at ~14,000 neurons per lane, QC sequencing on NextSeq 2000 P3 100-cycle then production sequencing on a NovaSeq6000 S2 flowcell

Human cortical organoid generation and transduction: HUES66-derived CHD8 and SCN2A mutant stem cells constitutively expressing dCas9-p300 (Addgene 83889) aggregated in Aggrewell 800, dual-SMAD plus XAV939 patterning, EGF/FGF then BDNF/NT3 maturation; three organoids per condition infected at MOI 5, collected 1 month post-infection, Trizol/PicoPure RNA isolation and Multiscribe cDNA synthesis

Patient iPSC lines: Cri-du-Chat (Cri1377, Cri1378) and Pitt-Hopkins (PH1, PH2) iPSCs maintained in StemFlex, transduced at MOI 100 with the all-in-one pLV VP64-dCas9-VP64 gRNA lentivirus, cultured 3 days and harvested in RLT lysis buffer with 2-mercaptoethanol

Humanized-Tcf4-Nanoluciferase knock-in mouse primary fibroblasts: plated at 5,000 cells/well (384-well, luminescence) or 25,000 cells/well (24-well, qRT-PCR), dosed 3 h after plating with dSpCas9-VP64 plus targeting or control gRNA lentivirus at MOI 50, cultured 7 days; Nano-Glo luminescence read on a BMG CLARIOstar Plus and qPCR on a QuantStudio 5

In vivo transgenic mouse embryo enhancer-activity assay: transgenic embryos generated by the technical team at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (acknowledged) to test autonomous cCRE activity in the developing mouse central nervous system; no bench protocol for this assay appears in the main-text Methods

headline.static_readiness: 0/17 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 2/17 computational steps (12%): C9 (MPRA DESeq2 analysis, R v3.4.2 / RStudio v2023.06.1+524 pinned, thresholds FDR < 0.01 and log2FC > 1 given, code deposited, data released) and C10 (CellRanger v7.0.1 against the GRCh38-3.0.0 reference, exact command-line files deposited, QC thresholds given, data released). Five further tools are pinned but sit in steps blocked on another axis: MPRAflow v2.3.5 (C7, C8 - no deposited workflow config, so code = 1), Bowtie2 v2.3.5.1 and Picard v2.26.0 (C2 - ENCODE pipelines unpinned, no script deposited, source data un-accessioned), Homer v5.1 (C13 - no Homer command file deposited). The remaining 12 steps cap at NI because no version is stated at all for denovolyzeR, ABC, liftOver, bedtools, FlashFry, DESeq2, SCEPTRE, snakemake, BSgenome, Gviz, bigWigAverageOverBed or R at those steps. No lockfile, container digest, conda environment.yml or renv.lock is claimed in the paper or the linked repository (25 files, no license, no release tag, no Zenodo DOI), so even at Stage 2 no step could exceed RI on environment grounds. Both figures under-claim by construction: Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency.
headline.coverage: 17 computational steps assessed from the main-text Methods prose plus the linked GitHub repository's file listing and README. 12 wet-lab steps (MPRA library cloning, piggyFlex gRNA library cloning, individual lentiviral gRNA cloning, HEK293T lentivirus production, NGN2-iNeuron differentiation for MPRA, nucleofection/selection/differentiation for the screen, lentiMPRA transduction and sequencing, 10x capture and sequencing, cerebral organoids, patient iPSC lines, humanized-hTcf4 mouse fibroblasts, transgenic mouse embryos) counted in W and out of computational-reproduction scope. Computational coverage = 17/29 (59%).

gaps.where: Environment closure across the whole paper and the whole repository
gaps.missing: No lockfile (renv.lock, conda-lock, pixi.lock), no conda environment.yml, no requirements.txt, no Dockerfile, no container image or digest, and no sessionInfo() dump appears in the paper or in github.com/shendurelab/Neural_CRE_MPRA_CRISPRa (25 files, all R/Rmd scripts, three CellRanger command-line text files, two FlashFry cluster config text files, a Snakefile, sm_script.sh and README.md). The repo has no license, no release tag and no Zenodo DOI, so there is not even a commit-pinned snapshot to reproduce against. Consequently every step is capped at version = 1 even if its tool is pinned exactly.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a renv.lock (the analysis is R-dominant) plus a conda-lock or container digest covering the non-R tools (CellRanger, MPRAflow/Nextflow, Homer, Bowtie2, Picard, bedtools, liftOver, ABC, FlashFry), and cut a tagged release with a Zenodo DOI cited from the Code availability statement.

gaps.where: 12 of 17 computational steps (C1, C3, C4, C5, C6, C11, C12, C14, C15, C16, C17, and partially C2)
gaps.missing: No version is stated for denovolyzeR, the ABC model code (MakeCandidateRegions.py / run.neighborhoods.py / predict.py), UCSC liftOver, bedtools, FlashFry, DESeq2, SCEPTRE, snakemake, the BSgenome package and its hg38 data package, Gviz, bigWigAverageOverBed, TrimGalore, or the ENCODE ATAC-seq/ChIP-seq pipelines. Exact pins exist for only seven items in the whole paper: Bowtie2 v2.3.5.1, Picard MarkDuplicates v2.26.0, MPRAflow v2.3.5, CellRanger v7.0.1 (plus the GRCh38-3.0.0 reference), R v3.4.2, RStudio v2023.06.1+524 and Homer v5.1. Steps with no version at all cannot reach RI.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a software-versions table to the Methods naming and pinning every tool, interpreter and R/Bioconductor package actually used, and state the R version separately for the single-cell arm (R v3.4.2 is stated only for the MPRA arm and is implausibly old for SCEPTRE, so the single-cell interpreter version is effectively unknown).

gaps.where: C2, C7, C8, C13, C14 - steps whose invocation is described in prose but whose script is not in the deposited repository
gaps.missing: The repository contains design, analysis and figure code but no artifact for: the ENCODE ATAC/ChIP alignment and TrimGalore/Bowtie2/Picard preprocessing that produces the ABC inputs (C2); the MPRAflow association.nf and count.nf invocations and their config/profile (C7, C8); the Homer findMotifsGenome.pl / annotatePeaks.pl commands (C13); and the bigWigAverageOverBed enrichment across 258 biochemical datasets (C14). Their flags are given in prose, so they are reconstructable, but not directly executable from the deposit.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the shell/Nextflow wrappers for these five steps alongside the R code, in the same style as the three CellRanger command-line files already provided.

gaps.where: C1, C2, C4, C14, C15, C17 - input datasets and validation measurements without accessions
gaps.missing: Newly generated data are well handled (IGVF portal accessions IGVFDS1120GRVG for MPRA and IGVFDS2290SSEF for the single-cell CRISPRa screen, both resolving with status 'released'). Reused and validation data are not: the de novo variant tables from 42,320 offspring (C1) are cited by literature reference only; the five enhancer-gene prediction datasets and the GW18 PFC / NGN2 ATAC, H3K27ac ChIP-seq and CUT&RUN inputs (C2, C4) are cited by reference with only one explicit accession among them (GSE113483 for the NGN2 pcHiC contacts); the 258 ATAC-seq and histone/TF ChIP-seq datasets used for biochemical enrichment (C14) have no per-dataset accession list; the VISTA transgenic-enhancer set (C15) has no release or retrieval date; and the raw qPCR Ct tables and luminescence readings underlying the validation figures (C17) are covered by neither IGVF accession.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a supplementary table listing an accession or DOI for every reused dataset (including all 258 biochemical tracks) and deposit the qPCR/luminescence source values as a supplementary data file.

gaps.where: External reference resources consumed by C1, C2, C3, C4, C6, C10, C13, C15, C16
gaps.missing: External resources are pinned in prose only or not at all: the Gencode 'basic annotation' used for promoter definition has no release number (C3); the hg19 and hg38 genome builds and the UCSC liftOver chain file have no version or download URL (C2, C4); the DDG2P Decipher gene list has no download date (C1); the FANTOM fetal-brain CAGE resource is given as a browser URL (https://fantom.gsc.riken.jp/5/sstar/FF:10085-102B4, HTTP 200) with no file version (C6); the Homer annotated-motif database has no release (C13); the VISTA Enhancer browser set has no version/date (C15); the RefSeq/ENSEMBL transcript annotation used for the Gviz tracks has no release (C16). The single well-pinned external resource is the CellRanger GRCh38-3.0.0 reference transcriptome (C10). At Stage 2 these would classify as Class B (prose-only pin) or worse.
gaps.how_to_close: Fetch each external resource through a versioned download rule inside the deposited Snakemake workflow, recording the release identifier, URL and a checksum for each.

gaps.where: Stochastic operations in C5, C12 (and the iterative selection in C6)
gaps.missing: No RNG seed is reported for the 'base-level shuffled versions of a randomly selected subset of the 44,312 tiles' used as MPRA negative controls (C5, which in turn sets the empirical 6.2% FDR quoted in C9), nor for the random downsampling of NTCs to match the number of targeting cis tests on the QQ plots (C12). SCEPTRE's own resampling-based calibration is also unseeded in the prose.
gaps.how_to_close: Set and record seeds in the deposited R scripts, or state explicitly that only distributional agreement is expected and ship the exact shuffled-control and downsampled-NTC sets as data files.

gaps.where: C2 - epigenomic read processing externalized by citation
gaps.missing: The entire ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq alignment sub-pipeline is delegated to 'the Encode Consortium ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq pipelines with default settings and pseudo replicate generation turned off', cited to a reference rather than to a pinned pipeline version, commit or container. The ENCODE pipelines' defaults have changed materially across releases, so 'default settings' is not a stable specification without the version.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the exact ENCODE pipeline release (e.g. atac-seq-pipeline vX.Y.Z) or its container digest, and ship the input JSON used.

gaps.where: Code availability statement and repository provenance
gaps.missing: The Code availability statement points to a bare repository URL ('Analysis and visualization code are available at GitHub (https://github.com/shendurelab/Neural_CRE_MPRA_CRISPRa/)') with no commit hash, no tag and no archival DOI; the repository itself carries no license file, no release, no tag and no CITATION file, and its README is the paper abstract plus a two-sentence contents note with no installation, dependency or execution instructions. The repository is live (HTTP 200, created 2025-09-01, last push 2025-10-24), but a reader has no way to obtain the exact state of the code used for the paper.
gaps.how_to_close: Tag the manuscript state, mint a Zenodo DOI, add an open-source license and a README section giving dependency installation and the intended execution order of the 25 scripts.

gaps.missing: CellRanger is vendor-distributed 10x Genomics software under a proprietary end-user license, not installable from a public package channel without accepting 10x terms; the same applies to the GRCh38-3.0.0 reference bundle. The version is pinned exactly, so this does not block RI at Stage 1, but it does block a fully open environment lock at Stage 2.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the CellRanger download URL and checksum, or supply the post-CellRanger filtered count matrix (already deposited under IGVFDS2290SSEF) as the reproducible entry point so the vendor-licensed step can be skipped.

gaps.missing: MPRA and gRNA library cloning, lentivirus production, iPSC and NGN2-iNeuron culture and differentiation, piggyBac nucleofection and selection, transduction, 10x Chromium capture, Illumina sequencing, cerebral organoid generation, patient iPSC lines, humanized-hTcf4 mouse fibroblasts and transgenic mouse embryo generation are physical data-generation steps, out of scope for computational reproduction; counted in W (12), not verdicted. Protocols are described in unusually complete detail (catalogue numbers, cycling conditions, MOIs), and the transgenic mouse embryo assay (W12) is the one exception with no bench protocol in the main-text Methods.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; the deposited IGVF file sets are the reproducible entry point for the computational arm.
